driver: The decisive quantity is a conversion rate from committed volume to realised cash recovered from a closed corpus of completed cases, and only the rate netted of reversals recorded on a separate ledger reproduces every case, because the transaction record is complete about inflows and structurally silent about clawbacks.
driver_concrete: RBDC's $56.8M beats AMRC's $38.9M by 1.46 only when exposure is converted at the 24-month rate net of in-window recapture from the certification register (23-14-071(c) keeps recapture off the claims extract), the one bridge that reproduces all four completed close-outs while every gross or rival window rule misses one by 42 percent or more.
stump: A solver who scores cash rather than exposure but measures the 24-month conversion off the claims extract alone, which never shows a recapture, files AMRC at $72.0M, the decoy the design-archetype shortcut and the analyst's 24 July read also reach; in-house rounds 6 and 7 both landed AMRC.
